reco_headline: On the labelled cash flows, the project clears a 10.96% CAPM WACC (NPV 0.71bn INR unhedged, 0.93bn on the forward path). The project ends after year 3 with zero salvage. Unhedged NPV reaches zero if every free cash flow is 8% lower. Those cash flows are a teaching case, not an Infosys forecast. Hedge year-1 receipts with a 25Δ collar, not a 100% forward, so a weaker rupee can still help. Both NPVs use the same WACC; the hedge changes the FX path only.
hedge_call: Prefer the 25Δ collar over 100% forwards: residual vol drops versus unhedged while keeping participation if USDINR rises (exporter-friendly). Use the Asian only if the desk will actually average monthly fixings; otherwise the vanilla put leg is cleaner.
notes: India 10Y FRED pull failed; using labelled fallback 6.50%.

strategy_used: monthly, long-only shrinkage mean-variance using trailing historical returns, with a 35% position cap
ml_verdict: ML-MV beat Nifty, but did not beat the simpler historical-MV rule; GB also failed to improve INFY forecast error (sign hit near 50%). The historical-MV rule is therefore selected, while ML stays as a documented challenger and robustness test.
debt_line: Reported debt is negligible, so WACC equals the cost of equity. The bond shows YTM and duration; it does not change this NPV.
